title: Uniform compact-support estimate for a submersion phase
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field], with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure. Let $n,k\geq1$, let $U\subset\mathbf R^n$ be open, let $C\subset U$ be compact, and let $H:U\to\mathbf R^k$ be smooth. Assume that the derivative $DH(z):\mathbf R^n\to\mathbf R^k$ is surjective for every $z\in U$. For an integer $N\geq0$ and a smooth function $u:U\to\mathbf C$ vanishing off $C$, put $$p_N(u)=\max_{|\alpha|\leq N}\sup_{z\in U}|\partial^\alpha u(z)|.$$ For every $N\geq0$ there is a finite constant $A_N\geq0$, depending only on $U,C,H,N$, such that for every such $u$ and every $\eta\in\mathbf R^k$, $$\left|\int_U e^{iH(z)\cdot\eta}u(z)\,dz\right|\leq A_N(1+|\eta|)^{-N}p_N(u).$$ If $C$ is empty, take $p_N(u)=0$.

source.place: Agent-supplied analytic prerequisite below the inherited global-quantization branch: compact nonlinear submersion-phase estimate, extending the integration-by-parts idea in Demailly course §3, estimate (3.11), printed p.9. The nonlinear estimate is not asserted to be stated in those notes. WANTED locally; supplemental notes read online: https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf.

proof.text: If $C=\varnothing$, then $u=0$ and take $A_N=0$. Henceforth $C\ne\varnothing$. Every derivative of $u$ vanishes on the open set $U\setminus C$, so its support is contained in $C$. Apply [lem-sfb-compact-continuous-norm-bound] to the real and imaginary parts of each $\partial^\alpha u$ on $C$, extended arbitrarily outside $U$. There are finitely many $|\alpha|\leq N$, so $p_N(u)$ is finite and nonnegative. Write $V=\operatorname{vol}(C)<\infty$; finiteness is the compact-measure clause of [lem-sfb-real-compact-supported-integral-bound]. Each smooth function supported in $C$ is integrable on $C$ by [lem-sfb-continuous-on-compact-integrable], and its integral on $U$ equals its integral on $C$.

source.place: Agent-written nonlinear extension of the integration-by-parts argument of Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §1 (1.7) and §3 (3.11), printed pp.2 and 9; supplemental notes read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. WANTED locally; the nonlinear assertion is not stated in those notes.

proof.text: For $\theta\in\mathbf R^k\setminus\{0\}$ set $g(z,\theta)=DH(z)^t\theta$ and $q(z,\theta)=\sum_jg_j(z,\theta)^2$. This is positive: if $g=0$, choose $w$ with $DH(z)w=\theta$ by surjectivity, obtaining $|\theta|^2=\theta\cdot DH(z)w=g\cdot w=0$, a contradiction. The components $g_j$ and $q$ are smooth on the open set $U\times(\mathbf R^k\setminus\{0\})$. Regard $q$ as complex-valued and apply [lem-sfb-smooth-nonzero-complex-reciprocal]. Thus $a_j=g_j/q$ are smooth real functions there. Put $\phi_\theta(z)=H(z)\cdot\theta$, $L_\theta=\sum_ja_j\partial_j$ and $T_\theta v=-\sum_j\partial_j(a_jv)$. The chain rule gives $L_\theta\phi_\theta=\sum_jg_j^2/q=1$ and $L_\theta(e^{-it\phi_\theta})=-it e^{-it\phi_\theta}$ for real $t$.

source.place: Agent-written nonlinear extension of the integration-by-parts argument of Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §1 (1.7) and §3 (3.11), printed pp.2 and 9; supplemental notes read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. WANTED locally; the nonlinear assertion is not stated in those notes.

proof.text: Fix $|\theta|=1$. Apply [lem-sfb-coordinate-weighted-adjoint] on $U$ with scalar ranks $r=s=1$, both Hermitian matrices and density equal to $1$, coefficients $A_j=a_j$ and $B=0$, first input $e^{-it\phi_\theta}$ and second input any smooth $v$ supported in $C$. The coefficients are real, so the displayed $Q$ of that node is exactly $T_\theta$. Only the second input needs compact support. Its pairing identity reads $$it\int_Ue^{it\phi_\theta}v=\int_Ue^{it\phi_\theta}T_\theta v.$$ Differentiation and multiplication do not enlarge the support, so $T_\theta^rv$ is smooth and supported in $C$ for every $r\geq0$. Starting with $r=0$ and applying this identity to $v=T_\theta^ru$ proves by induction $$ (it)^N\int_Ue^{it\phi_\theta}u=\int_Ue^{it\phi_\theta}T_\theta^Nu.$$

source.place: Agent-written nonlinear extension of the integration-by-parts argument of Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §1 (1.7) and §3 (3.11), printed pp.2 and 9; supplemental notes read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. WANTED locally; the nonlinear assertion is not stated in those notes.

proof.text: Here is the coefficient induction, including its uniformity. Set $c_{0,0}=1$ and all other $c_{0,\alpha}=0$. For absent indices put $c_{r,\alpha}=0$ and define $$c_{r+1,\beta}=-\sum_{j=1}^n\bigl[\partial_j(a_jc_{r,\beta})+a_jc_{r,\beta-e_j}\bigr],$$ with negative multi-indices interpreted as zero. The product rule proves, by induction on $r$, $$T_\theta^ru=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq r}c_{r,\alpha}(z,\theta)\partial^\alpha u(z).$$ All coefficients are jointly smooth, since the recursion only differentiates, adds and multiplies the smooth $a_j$. The unit sphere $S\subset\mathbf R^k$ is compact by [lem-cbc-euclidean-sphere-compact], and $C\times S$ is compact by the following finite-cover argument. Refine any open cover at each $(z,\theta)$ to product neighborhoods. For fixed $z$, finitely many second-factor neighborhoods cover $S$; intersect their first-factor neighborhoods to obtain $V_z$. Finitely many $V_z$ cover $C$, and the corresponding finitely many original cover elements cover $C\times S$. Apply [lem-sfb-compact-continuous-norm-bound] to every $c_{N,\alpha}$ on this subset of $\mathbf R^{n+k}$, extending it arbitrarily off its open domain. Choose nonnegative bounds $b_{N,\alpha}$ and put $B_N=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq N}b_{N,\alpha}$. The finite displayed sum gives $$|T_\theta^Nu(z)|\leq B_Np_N(u)\quad(z\in C,\ |\theta|=1).$$ The coefficients and their bounds depend only on $H,U,C,N$, never on $u,t$.

source.place: Agent-written nonlinear extension of the integration-by-parts argument of Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §1 (1.7) and §3 (3.11), printed pp.2 and 9; supplemental notes read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. WANTED locally; the nonlinear assertion is not stated in those notes.

proof.text: Let $t=|\eta|\geq1$ and $\theta=\eta/t$. Then $H(z)\cdot\eta=t\phi_\theta(z)$. On $C$ the integrand on the right of the induction identity has absolute value at most $B_Np_N(u)$, since $|e^{it\phi_\theta}|=1$. Apply [lem-sfb-integrable-majorant-estimate] for Lebesgue measure restricted to $C$, with the constant integrable majorant $B_Np_N(u)$. (Its integral is $VB_Np_N(u)$, because $V<\infty$.) Taking absolute values in that identity gives $$\left|\int_Ue^{iH\cdot\eta}u\right|\leq VB_Nt^{-N}p_N(u)\leq2^NVB_N(1+t)^{-N}p_N(u).$$ The last inequality is $1+t\leq2t$. This includes $N=0$.

source.place: Agent-written nonlinear extension of the integration-by-parts argument of Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §1 (1.7) and §3 (3.11), printed pp.2 and 9; supplemental notes read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. WANTED locally; the nonlinear assertion is not stated in those notes.

proof.text: For $0\leq t=|\eta|\leq1$, use [lem-sfb-integrable-majorant-estimate] on $C$ with constant majorant $p_0(u)$ to get $|\int_Ue^{iH\cdot\eta}u|\leq Vp_0(u)\leq Vp_N(u)$. Since $(1+t)^N\leq2^N$, this is at most $2^NV(1+t)^{-N}p_N(u)$. Together with the previous step, $A_N=2^NV\max(1,B_N)$ proves the required estimate for every $\eta$, including $\eta=0$. It remains valid if $V=0$ or $u=0$.
